P1.evidence: The phase never happened. The first roughly ten minutes went entirely to Zoom camera troubleshooting and small talk about Bulgaria, fruit trees and grandchildren, and the rep then slid straight into nutrition questions at 00:09:58 with 'okay, I've heard a few things.' No setter notes or application were read back - the rep did not even know the prospect had already asked about price ('Oh, you haven't seen a response to that?'). No frame, no frame agreement, and no 'what are you potentially looking for help with' - the prospect volunteered his reason for being there unprompted at 00:05:00.

P2.evidence: Age, height and weight all asked. Work covered well, including shift pattern and hours ('what times do you specifically work?'). Injuries and mobility asked directly: 'how is your mobility like at the moment? Do you have stiffnesses, injuries that we should know about?' Nutrition probed properly with an honesty check. But health conditions and hereditary risk were never asked - the multigenerational cancer history, the no-medication status and the prescribed sleep aid were all volunteered. Sleep is the biggest miss: the prospect delivered a two-minute unprompted account of twelve years of chronic sleep deprivation and the rep neither asked about it beforehand nor followed up on it. Energy never asked. Current training was established as effectively zero, so results-from-training does not apply.

P3.evidence: Good work at the deep end. 'Describe me that version of Rob that is in shape again in like six months or a year from now' opened it, 'Why is it so important for you, Rob, to actually take action on it this time' bridged past the physical, and 'how would that be for you as a person, Rob, when you finally get back to that after years of not being in that shape' landed the future-self question. The drive-through reached kids, grandkids, the pool, his daughter's October wedding and the family cancer lineage. Weaknesses: the goals menu was replaced by a single open 'any other goals besides just the physical appearance aspect' which got a flat no; there was no 'something physical you want to do but can't'; the impact-on-others question was asserted rather than asked ('It sounds like when you work on that, that's going to enable you to inspire your kids'); and the reflect-back never reached the scripted form - the nearest was 'It sounds like you want to be a success story', which is about commitment rather than the real why.

P4.evidence: The strongest single moment of the call was a direct, honest challenge: 'you've got a gym that you can go to, you have a home gym, you don't use it, you've got some kettlebells that have been collecting dust, and I just want to be completely honest. Like, doesn't sound like it's the biggest priority. So why are you choosing to now actually take a step?' That is P4c done properly. The gap was then named and confirmed - the rep summarised 'it comes down to having accountability, having a routine in place, actually have someone sort of giving you the guidance' and got 'Yes, yes, yes, Richard.' But the past attempts themselves were mostly volunteered rather than asked for, the one-thing-in-the-way question was never put directly, and the 'the information isn't the problem, why can't you stick to it on your own' line never ran.

P5.evidence: Ran nearly in full. 'When it continues like this and you're 65... How would you look back at this current moment in four years if you haven't actually done something?' got 'that's totally unacceptable.' The settle question was put, if as a leading statement: 'that will probably tell you right now that you're absolutely not willing to settle for that life, is it?' The line in the sand was drawn explicitly and a promise extracted: 'when you draw that line in the sand, you actually step over it, you're not going to quit... Can you promise yourself that?' 'Yes, I can.' Only the 'why not' follow-up was skipped.

P6.evidence: 'Do you believe in yourself that you can get back into that state where you were in sort of before you were married... do you believe in yourself that you can make that work?' followed by 'do you feel like there is anything internally for you that would stop you from actually committing to it and sticking with it for the rest of your life?' Both answered yes and no respectively. Discipline on P6c was good: having got the yes, the rep correctly declined to present because the decision needed the wife in the room.

P11.evidence: No offer was presented and no close was attempted. The rep deliberately parked the presentation for a joint call with the prospect's wife on Friday: 'then she can actually see me, I can explain the whole process to the two of you, and then we'll get started with you.' The phase was unreachable on this call.

objection_plays.detail: The money signal was clear and early - 'we all have to pay bills... as I transition and retire, of course, the budget is going to be a lot tighter' - and none of the play ran. No isolate, no SHOULD-I-versus-HOW reframe, no offer to explore breaking it up, no permission question, and none of the six financial-picture questions. Worse than a miss on the play: the rep pre-empted it by volunteering a price range before any value had been built, which is the opposite of the scripted sequence.

The trigger landed cleanly at 00:41:19. None of the six scripted moves ran - no 'money aside, do you personally feel this CAN get you there', no 'what obstacles might come up', no 'is there any reason she would NOT want you healthier', no permission-versus-input reframe, no deposit. The rep instead substituted a different play entirely: bring her onto the next call. Given she 'thinks I'm on a scam phone call right now' that was arguably the better commercial judgement, but it is off-script and it hands the decision to a second call with the offer still unpresented.

The prospect raised and half-pre-empted the not-yet objection himself: 'I'm going to be retiring in October and I hate to use that as an excuse and wait till then.' The rep caught it immediately with 'Are you willing to also carve out that time at the moment?' which is the right instinct, and later reinforced it with the four-years-from-now question. But the scripted moves - things never slow down, the longer you wait the harder this gets, all you have to do is show up - were not used, and the October retirement was allowed to stand as the implicit start line.

Script gap. A 61-year-old with self-reported BMI over 30, twelve years of chronic sleep deprivation on a prescribed sleep aid that does not work, and a stated refusal of conventional oncology in favour of homeopathic protocols, was moved toward starting kettlebell training. There is no step anywhere in the process for medication review, clinical clearance, or for handling a prospect who volunteers distrust of conventional medicine, so the rep had nothing to run and simply moved past all of it.

notes: Genuinely strong in the middle - Phase 5 ran almost complete, the commitment check was clean, and the dusty-kettlebells challenge in Phase 4 was the best coaching moment in the batch. It is bookended by two structural failures: no opening frame at all after ten minutes lost to Zoom troubleshooting, and an unsolicited invented price range delivered at minute fourteen before any value existed. Coach him to hold price until the presentation and to run the frame even when the call starts messily.
